learning: If the score returns to about 69 with line loss at or below 1 per run, kd has little effect and the next lever is line-loss handling. If the score rises above 69.32, keep kd 0.2 and test a further small decrease. If the score falls or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15, return kd to 0.3.
notes: Reference geometry (iteration 1 values, reproduced in iterations 4 and 6) with kd lowered from 0.3 to 0.2 as the only change. Reverses the kd 0.4 test in iteration 8, which scored 56.44.
rationale: The reference geometry (iterations 1, 4, 6: 69.32, reproducible) is held unchanged, as the Builder proposed. Controller evidence so far: kd 0.4 (iteration 8) scored 56.44, down 12.9 points, with steering_oscillation rising to 0.14 on s-bend and slalom and no drop in line loss. base_speed 1.15 (iteration 7) scored 61.77, with oval line loss rising to 1.45. Every controller change tested so far has lowered the score, and line loss has stayed near 1 per run under every geometry. Since kd went up and lost ground, the single untested direction on this gain is down. This iteration therefore tests kd 0.2, with every other value at the iteration 1 reference (base_speed 1.3, kp 2.5, ki 0, last_direction, weights -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1). Sign check: positive x (left) has a positive weight, so a line on the left steers left, as the contract requires. Expected result: a score near 69 if kd has little effect, or a gain if less derivative damping helps. This is a prediction, not a measurement. If the score falls below 69, kd 0.3 is the best-supported value and the next test should be line-loss handling rather than gain tuning.
